```{=typst}
#let mk(n) = box(baseline: 22%, circle(radius: 5.8pt, fill: rgb("#d9480f"), stroke: none, inset: 0pt)[#set align(center + horizon); #text(fill: white, weight: "bold", size: 8pt)[#n]])
#let tick = box(baseline: 12%, width: 10pt, height: 10pt, stroke: 0.9pt + luma(70), radius: 2pt)
#let shot(path, w: 100%) = block(breakable: false, stroke: 0.8pt + luma(150), radius: 6pt, clip: true, image(path, width: w))
#let typebox(body) = block(width: 100%, breakable: false, fill: rgb("#f1f6fd"), stroke: 0.8pt + rgb("#185abd"), radius: 5pt, inset: (x: 12pt, y: 9pt), body)
#let tip(body) = block(width: 100%, breakable: false, fill: rgb("#fff4e6"), stroke: (left: 3pt + rgb("#d9480f")), inset: (x: 10pt, y: 7pt), radius: 3pt, body)
// One step: the box to tick, its number and what to do on the left; its screen on the right.
#let step(n, body, img: none, w: 100%, left: 40%, after: none) = block(breakable: false, above: 9pt, below: 9pt, width: 100%)[
  #set par(justify: false, leading: 0.62em)
  #let words = grid(columns: (auto, 1fr), column-gutter: 6pt, [#tick #h(1pt) *#n.*], body)
  #if img == none { words } else {
    grid(columns: (left, 1fr), column-gutter: 12pt, align: (top, top), words, align(center, shot(img, w: w)))
  }
  #if after != none { v(4pt); after }
]
```

::: {.lead}
Today you make a small database in **Access** on the lab computer: a table of customers and a query. Do the tasks in order. The **orange
numbers** in each picture show where to click. Tick the box `#tick`{=typst} after each step. Stuck? Raise your hand.
:::

- **You need:** a lab computer with Access. **Nothing to download:**
  you type the text yourself.
- **Time:** about 35 minutes. Your Access may look a little different:
  the names of the buttons are the same.

## Task 1 · Open Access and make a database

```{=typst}
#step(1, [Click *Search* on the taskbar #mk(1). Type *access*. Click *Access* #mk(2).], img: "images/lab-open-1.png", w: 80%, left: 32%)
#step(2, [Click *Blank database* #mk(1). \ In *File Name*, type *shop-* and your first name #mk(2). \ Click *Create* #mk(3). A table, *Table1*, opens.], img: "images/lab-new-1.png", w: 92%, left: 36%)
```

```{=typst}
#pagebreak(weak: true)
```

## Task 2 · The fields of the table

```{=typst}
#step(1, [On the *Home* tab, click *View ▾* #mk(1), then *Design View* #mk(2). \ Type the table name: #h(3pt) #box(fill: white, stroke: 0.6pt + rgb("#185abd"), radius: 4pt, inset: 4pt)[Customers] #mk(3). Click *OK* #mk(4).], img: "images/lab-design-1.png", w: 100%, left: 36%)
#step(2, [Under *ID*, type the field name *Name* #mk(1); its data type: *Short Text* #mk(2). \ Then the field *City*, *Short Text*. \ The small key #mk(3): *ID* is the primary key.], img: "images/lab-fields-1.png", w: 100%, left: 36%)
```

## Task 3 · Three customers

```{=typst}
#step(1, [Click *View* #mk(1) (Datasheet View). Click *Yes* to save. \ Type three customers #mk(2): Name, *Tab*, City, *Tab*: \ #box(fill: white, stroke: 0.6pt + rgb("#185abd"), radius: 4pt, inset: 5pt)[Huda · Amman \ Omar · Irbid \ Rana · Amman] \ ID counts by itself.], img: "images/lab-records-1.png", w: 100%, left: 40%)
```

```{=typst}
#pagebreak(weak: true)
```

## Task 4 · A query: the customers in Amman

```{=typst}
#step(1, [Click the *Create* tab #mk(1). Click *Query Design* #mk(2). \ Add *Customers* (double-click it, then close the list). \ Double-click *Name*, then *City* #mk(3).], img: "images/lab-query-1.png", w: 100%, left: 36%)
#step(2, [Under *Name*, *Sort*: *Ascending* #mk(1). \ Under *City*, *Criteria*: type *Amman* #mk(2). \ Click *Run* #mk(3): Huda and Rana. \ Press *Ctrl + S*, type #h(2pt) #box(fill: white, stroke: 0.6pt + rgb("#185abd"), radius: 4pt, inset: 4pt)[Amman customers], *OK*.], img: "images/lab-query-2.png", w: 100%, left: 36%)
```

## Task 5 · Export the table to Excel

Access saves your database by itself. For the Extra, you save the table as an Excel file too.

```{=typst}
#step(1, [On the left, right-click *Customers* #mk(1). \ Click *Export* #mk(2), then *Excel* #mk(3). \ Click *OK*, then *Close*. The file *Customers.xlsx* is in *Documents*.], img: "images/lab-export-1.png", w: 100%, left: 34%)
```

## Extra · AI adds customers to your table

```{=typst}
#block(width: 100%, fill: rgb("#e3f4f1"), stroke: 0.8pt + rgb("#8fd1c4"), radius: 6pt, inset: (x: 12pt, y: 9pt))[
  Only when you finish Tasks 1–5. On *tutudocs.com* an *AI assistant* changes your table (Customers.xlsx) for you. *No sign-in.*
]
#step(1, [Open the browser. Go to *tutudocs.com*.])
#step(2, [Click the box *Drop a file anywhere on this page, or click to choose* #mk(1). \ Click *Documents*, click your file *Customers.xlsx*, click *Open*. \ Your table opens in the online editor.], img: "images/lab-tutu-1.png", w: 84%, left: 36%)
#step(3, [Click *AI Assistant* at the top #mk(1). \ Click in *Ask AI anything…* #mk(2) and type: #h(3pt) #box(fill: white, stroke: 0.6pt + rgb("#8fd1c4"), radius: 4pt, inset: 5pt)[Add 3 customers with a name and a city in Jordan.] \ Press *Enter* #mk(3). Wait about 15 seconds: three new customers come.], after: align(center, shot("images/lab-tutu-2.png", w: 84%)))
#step(4, [One more request. Type: #h(3pt) #box(fill: white, stroke: 0.6pt + rgb("#8fd1c4"), radius: 4pt, inset: 5pt)[Sort the customers by City, A to Z.] \ Press *Enter*. Wait for the answer before you type again.])
#step(5, [Click *File* #mk(1), then *Download* #mk(2), then the choice that ends in *.xlsx* #mk(3). \ Open the new file from *Downloads*: it opens in Excel, with the changes of the AI.], img: "images/lab-tutu-3.png", w: 74%, left: 44%)
```
